title: Can sides of three, three and seven make a triangle?
description: The longest side of seven centimetres is compared with the other two sides added together, and the result is checked by drawing arcs from the ends of a base. Keeko doubts the result and says the lengths can be changed round to make a triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the longest side must be less than the other two added together, whatever order the lengths are written in. Watch for children who think moving the lengths to different sides of a rough triangle can fix the problem.

source: Can we say anything about the existence of a triangle having sidelengths 3 cm, 3 cm and 7 cm? Verify your answer by construction.
video_script.why: The child has tested lengths by comparing direct and roundabout paths and now tests a new set and checks it with arcs.
video_script.substitution: The direct path is the longest side of seven centimetres and the roundabout path is the other two sides, three plus three centimetres.
video_script.anchor: A rough triangle with sides of three, three and seven centimetres
video_script.wrong_answer: change the order of the lengths
video_script.wrong_move: A child tries to place the seven centimetre length on a different side of the rough triangle, hoping the comparison will then come out fine.
video_script.payoff_line: No triangle exists for three, three and seven centimetres.

final_answer.spoken: no triangle exists for three, three and seven centimetres

never_show: the words no triangle before the answer beat
maths_rules: direct AB = 7 cm; roundabout AC + CB = 3 + 3 = 6 cm
7 > 6, so the direct path is longer than the roundabout path, which cannot be
base AB = 7 cm; arcs of 3 cm from A and from B cover 3 + 3 = 6 cm of the 7 cm and leave a gap of 1 cm, so they do not meet
the longest length is 7 in any order and the other two still add to 6
video_script.design: One idea: the longest side must be less than the other two added together. One rough triangle, one comparison and one construction check; Keeko's doubt closes the video.
